subject: Materials Science
title: N-Type Doping: Adding Electrons
description: One-minute skill: N-Type Doping: Adding Electrons.

hook.text: Add one phosphorus atom per million silicon atoms and conductivity jumps a thousandfold.

buildup.text: Phosphorus has five valence electrons — four bond with silicon, one is left over as a free carrier.

discovery.text: That extra electron sits just below the conduction band — easily excited at room temperature.

twist.text: The crystal stays electrically neutral — the extra electron is balanced by the phosphorus nucleus's extra proton.

climax.text: N-type silicon is used in every MOSFET source and drain — the building block of digital logic.

punchline.text: One extra electron per million atoms rewrites the material's electrical destiny.

quiz.question: Why does phosphorus create n-type silicon?
options: It removes electrons from silicon atoms
Its fifth valence electron becomes a free carrier in the lattice
